terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build the morning round here and run it. Ctrl+C stops a program that never ends.

tasks.title: List the clocks to wind
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/rounds.cpp`, use a loop to print one line for each clock to wind, numbered from 1 up to `clocksToWind`:

```
Wind clock 1
Wind clock 2
...
Wind clock 5
```

Check runs your program with other numbers of clocks, 0 and 1 among them, and compares every line your task printed.
nextSteps: Write a `for` loop with a counter that starts at 1.
Decide the condition that lets the counter reach `clocksToWind`, and no further.
Print the line inside the loop's `{ }`, with the counter.
Build, run, and count the lines. Set `clocksToWind` to 0 for a moment and run again.
hints: A `for` loop has three parts in its round brackets: where the counter starts, the condition to go on, and what changes each time round.
The clocks are numbered from 1, and the last one is `clocksToWind` itself, so the condition has to let the counter be equal to it.
The shape is `for (int clock = 1; clock <= clocksToWind; clock++) { ... }`.

tasks.title: Count the strikes
tasks.description:
A striking clock strikes once at one o'clock, twice at two, and so on. Under `// Task 2`, make an `int` called `strikes` and, with a loop, add up the strikes of every hour from `fromHour` to `toHour`, both included. Print it once, after the loop:

```
Strikes: 78
```

Check runs your program with other hours, reads `strikes` and compares the line.
nextSteps: Make `strikes` before the loop, starting at 0.
Loop over the hours from `fromHour` to `toHour`.
Inside the loop, add the hour to `strikes`.
Print the line after the loop, then build and run.
hints: A running total is a variable made before the loop that grows a little each time round.
At three o'clock the clock strikes three times, so each time round the loop adds the hour itself. A variable made inside the loop starts again each time round and is gone after it.
The shape is `int strikes = 0;`, then `for (int hour = fromHour; hour <= toHour; hour++) { strikes += hour; }`.

tasks.title: Add up the serial number
tasks.description:
The maker's check number is the digits of the serial number added up: for 48213 it is 4+8+2+1+3. Under `// Task 3`, make an `int` called `digitSum` and work it out from `serialNumber` with a `while` loop. Print it:

```
Check number: 18
```

Check runs your program with other serial numbers, 0 among them, reads `digitSum` and compares the line.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on `/` and `%` with 10 again.
Make `digitSum` at 0, and a copy of the serial number to take digits from.
Write a `while` loop that goes on while digits are left, and inside it add the last digit and take it off.
Build and run. If it never ends, press Ctrl+C and look at what changes inside the loop.
hints: `% 10` gives the last digit of a whole number, and `/ 10` takes the last digit off: 482 / 10 is 48.
Each time round, add the last digit to `digitSum` and take it off the number. When the number reaches 0, no digits are left. If the number never changes, the loop never ends.
The shape is `while (rest > 0) { digitSum += rest % 10; rest /= 10; }`, with `rest` a copy of `serialNumber`.

tasks.title: Fit springs until the box is empty
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make an `int` called `springsLeft`, starting at `springsInBox`. Go through the waiting clocks, numbered from 1 up to `clocksWaiting`. Each clock takes `springsPerClock` springs: take them from `springsLeft` and print `Clock 1: fitted`. When there are not enough springs left for a clock, print `Out of springs at clock 4` and stop going through the clocks:

```
Clock 1: fitted
Clock 2: fitted
Clock 3: fitted
Out of springs at clock 4
```

Check runs your program with other boxes and clocks, one with exactly enough springs among them, reads `springsLeft` and compares every line.
nextSteps: Make `springsLeft`, then loop over the clocks from 1 to `clocksWaiting`.
Inside, first ask whether the springs left are enough for this clock.
When they are not, print the line and leave the loop.
Otherwise take the springs and print the fitted line. Build and run with a few boxes.
hints: `break` leaves the loop at once, and the program goes on after its `}`.
A clock can be fitted when the springs left are exactly enough, so the box runs out only when fewer are left than one clock takes. Ask before you take any.
The shape is `if (springsLeft < springsPerClock) { ...; break; }`, then `springsLeft -= springsPerClock;` and the fitted line.
